decisions.decision: How should predictions run on production cameras?
decisions.context: Inspection must continue when network access is unavailable. Predictions are needed at the line, so serving should be local.
decisions.rationale: Offline operation decides the choice: local serving keeps inspection available without network access, at the cost of maintaining a local service.
consequences: Each device needs a compatible model runtime.
Model updates must reach devices locally.

decisions.decision: How should the application integrate the model?
decisions.context: The model runs with the inspection application on devices with limited infrastructure. A separate service would add deployment and network dependencies.

alternatives.label: Model as module in modular monolith
cons: Small team: application and model releases are coupled

alternatives.label: Model as a service
pros: Small team: model has a service boundary
cons: Offline: service availability must be maintained

chosen.label: Model as module in modular monolith

decisions.rationale: Offline operation and budget decide for a model module in the application, giving up independent model-service deployment.
consequences: Application packages must include the model and runtime.
Model updates follow the device application release path.

decisions.decision: When and how should models be trained?
decisions.context: Newly labelled images arrive weekly, and the brief does not require learning from each image as it arrives. Training can happen centrally, apart from offline inference.

alternatives.label: Batch-based learning
cons: Weekly retraining: changes wait for the next run

alternatives.label: Incremental learning
pros: Weekly retraining: can incorporate new data continuously
cons: Budget: requires an ongoing training path

decisions.rationale: Tight budget decides for batch training on the weekly cadence; this gives up immediate use of newly labelled images.
consequences: Training requires a weekly data and compute window.
Validated model artifacts need a delivery path to devices.

decisions.decision: How should training data be versioned?
decisions.context: Weekly retraining depends on labelled images, and reproducibility requires identifying which data produced each model. Dedicated version support costs additional setup and upkeep.

alternatives.label: Data version repository
cons: Small team: adds a repository to maintain

alternatives.label: No data versioning
cons: Reproducibility: training inputs are harder to recover

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides for explicit data versioning, accepting its maintenance cost so a model can be linked to its training data.
consequences: Dataset versions and model artifacts need linked identifiers.
The team must maintain versioned data storage.

decisions.decision: How should weekly integration and delivery be automated?
decisions.context: A small team needs a repeatable way to package and push weekly model updates. Automation reduces manual work but takes initial setup.

alternatives.label: CI/CD pipeline
cons: Budget: requires pipeline setup and upkeep

alternatives.label: Build and Deployment scripts
cons: Small team: more manual release coordination

alternatives.label: No integration or delivery automation
cons: Weekly retraining: manual deployments add effort

decisions.rationale: The small-team driver decides for automated delivery, trading setup and upkeep for repeatable weekly packaging and deployment.
consequences: The pipeline needs checks before device rollout.
Offline devices require a staged transfer mechanism.

decisions.context: The brief specifies a weekly retraining rhythm. A scheduled trigger matches that cadence without needing devices to report new data or performance over a network.

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger
pros: Weekly retraining: matches a fixed cadence
cons: Small team: schedule and failures need oversight

alternatives.label: On availability of new training data trigger
pros: Weekly retraining: reacts when new images arrive
cons: Offline operation: depends on data availability signals

decisions.rationale: The specified weekly cadence decides for a schedule, trading immediate response to new data for a predictable, simple trigger.
consequences: Missed runs need detection and recovery.
Label arrival timing may delay retraining until the next scheduled run.

decisions.decision: How should a deployed model be rolled back?
decisions.context: Models are pushed to devices and may need to be replaced if a release causes problems. Keeping a previous version available supports recovery, with storage and rollout overhead.

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Reliable inspection: supports recovery from a bad release
cons: Offline operation: rollback packages must be available on devices

alternatives.label: Single model in production
pros: Budget: keeps only one active version
cons: Reliable inspection: recovery requires another deployment

decisions.rationale: Reliable inspection decides for retaining a rollback path, giving up device storage and package management simplicity.
consequences: Devices need access to a prior known-good artifact.
Rollout and rollback state must be tracked per device.

decisions.decision: How should training and labelled images be stored?
decisions.context: Retraining uses newly labelled images, so training needs a durable place to access them. The brief does not specify a shared or networked store, and devices may be offline.

alternatives.label: Shared data store
pros: Weekly retraining: provides a common training dataset
cons: Offline operation: store access may be unavailable at devices

alternatives.label: No data store
cons: Weekly retraining: organizing inputs becomes manual

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining decides for a shared training store, accepting infrastructure cost to centralize labelled images; the design space does not establish a storage topology suited to offline devices.
consequences: Training infrastructure needs access to the shared store.
Device-side inspection must not depend on that store.

decisions.decision: How should model quality be monitored in production?
decisions.context: Models run on devices that may be offline, limiting centralized observation. Some monitoring is needed to detect degradation, but the brief gives no telemetry budget or connectivity assumptions.

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
cons: Offline operation: metrics may not reach a central monitor

alternatives.label: No in-production monitoring
cons: Reliable inspection: degradation may go undetected

decisions.rationale: Reliable inspection decides for monitoring, giving up some budget to detect quality degradation; collection and transfer during offline periods remain unresolved.
consequences: Monitoring needs a way to measure model quality.
Offline periods require deferred reporting or local review.
